claims.title: Colleague shift responses may be intercepted on the unverified public-app channel
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts`, an on-path attacker between a colleague's phone and `process:scheduling-web-app` can intercept the colleague's shift response and its PII. This is conditional: the flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:internal-network`, but transport protection is unverified. The disclosed schedule can enable targeted social engineering against the colleague or staff operations.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` crosses a trust boundary but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown, while an attacker still needs an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII in a colleague's own shift information.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` to TLS 1.2+ and verify the web application's certificate.

claims.title: Store rota updates may be intercepted on the unverified manager-app channel
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, an on-path attacker can read rota entries for a store while a manager builds or changes them at `process:scheduling-web-app`. This is conditional on the unresolved transport control on a crossing from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:internal-network`. The exposed rota and staff information can be used to target colleagues and reveal operational staffing patterns.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` is a boundary crossing with unknown `encryption_in_transit`, although observation still requires a network-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical rota information.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, including certificate validation by manager clients.

claims.title: Rota requests may expose staff data if the app-service hop is unencrypted
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`, an attacker with a foothold on the internal path can intercept rota reads and writes between `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service`. The unresolved control could expose PII and rota data beyond the colleague or manager making a request. The captured identifiers and schedules can subsequently be used to target records handled by `store:rota-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_in_transit` of `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`; an attacker needs an internal on-path foothold. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical rota reads and writes.

mitigations.summary: Use mutually authenticated encryption between app and service
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests` to mTLS so rota payloads are confidential and both service peers are authenticated.

claims.title: Rota database traffic may expose colleague records if the service-store hop is unencrypted
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`, an attacker observing the internal database path can intercept rota entries, colleague names, contact details, and availability from `store:rota-database`. This is conditional on the unknown transport setting. The disclosure supplies a corpus of staff PII and operational data that can enable targeted fraud or social engineering.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas` has unknown `encryption_in_transit` and requires an internal on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries the rota database's PII, including contact details and availability, plus business-critical rota data.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server verification, preferably mTLS, for `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`.

claims.title: Payroll exports may be intercepted while written to the file share
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:file-share>write-payroll-export`, an attacker on the internal path can intercept the weekly payroll export before it reaches `store:file-share`. This is conditional on the unresolved transport control. The attacker obtains payroll PII and can use it to target the payroll collection process or affected colleagues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on unknown `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:file-share>write-payroll-export`; exploitation requires an internal path position. Impact is medium because the weekly payroll export carries PII.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt payroll-export delivery to the share
mitigations.detail: Use TLS or an authenticated encrypted file-transfer protocol for `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:file-share>write-payroll-export`.

claims.title: Payroll export collection may expose PII across the team boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`, an on-path attacker can intercept the weekly payroll export as `entity:payroll-system` collects it from `store:file-share`. This is conditional on the unknown transport control on the crossing between `boundary:payroll-team-environment` and `boundary:internal-network`. The export's PII can enable attacks against colleagues and payroll operations outside the scheduling environment.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` crosses a trust boundary with unknown `encryption_in_transit`, though an attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because the collected payroll export contains PII.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with authenticated endpoints for `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` and verify the payroll system's certificate or workload identity.

claims.title: A copied rota database may disclose all colleague records if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:rota-database` holds rota entries, colleague names, contact details, and availability. If its unknown `encryption_at_rest` value resolves to no effective encryption, an attacker holding a storage copy, such as a decommissioned volume, snapshot, or operational backup of this store, can read the records without using `process:scheduling-service`. This is a conditional disclosure finding, not an assertion that encryption is absent. A complete staff-data copy can enable broad targeted social engineering and operational profiling.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` of `store:rota-database`; a storage copy is a prerequisite, but unverified at-rest protection may leave it directly readable. Impact is medium because the store holds colleague PII, including contact details and availability, and business-critical rota data.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for rota database copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:rota-database`, then use managed-key encryption for the primary store and every backup, snapshot, replica, and decommissioned medium.
Limit export, snapshot, backup, and key-use permissions to dedicated operational principals and audit their use.

claims.title: A copied payroll file share may disclose exports if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: If the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value on `store:file-share` resolves to no effective encryption, an attacker who obtains a copy of its storage media or an operational copy can read weekly payroll exports without authenticating as `entity:payroll-system`. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest control. The copied export exposes colleague PII and can be used for payroll-themed impersonation and targeted fraud.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` of `store:file-share`; obtaining a storage copy is required, but an unencrypted copy would be directly readable. Impact is medium because the store contains weekly payroll exports with PII.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the file share and its operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:file-share` encryption at rest and require managed-key encryption for the share, backups, snapshots, and retained export copies.

mitigations.summary: Limit export retention and storage access
mitigations.detail: Restrict file-share and backup access to the payroll workflow's required principals and remove payroll exports after their approved retention period.

claims.title: Code in the scheduling service can read the rota database through its existing access
claims.description: `process:scheduling-service` reads and writes `store:rota-database` through `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`. An attacker who gains code execution in `process:scheduling-service` can use that component's existing database path to read rota entries and colleague details. The database-flow authentication is unknown, so the identity, scope, and isolation of this read access are not verified. The resulting staff-data corpus can be used for targeting colleagues and identifying sensitive availability patterns; encryption at rest would not protect against reads performed through an authorized service connection.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first run code in the internal `process:scheduling-service`, and no entry point or compromise path is stated. Impact is medium because that process reads `store:rota-database`, which holds colleague PII and business-critical rota data.

mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated database principal restricted to the rows and columns needed by `process:scheduling-service`, and document the authentication used on `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`.
Audit and alert on bulk or unusual reads by the scheduling service's database identity.

claims.title: Code in the payroll system can read exports through the file-share collection path
claims.description: `entity:payroll-system` reads `store:file-share` through `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`. An attacker controlling code in that payroll system can collect the weekly payroll export through its existing read path. Authentication on that flow is unknown, so the identity verification and scope of access remain unverified. The obtained payroll PII can enable targeted fraud against colleagues and attacks on associated payroll processes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first control `entity:payroll-system`, an external system in `boundary:payroll-team-environment`. Impact is medium because its existing collection flow reads a weekly payroll export containing PII from `store:file-share`.

mitigations.summary: Use a narrowly scoped payroll collection identity
mitigations.detail: Require a dedicated authenticated workload identity for `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`, limited to the current export and unable to enumerate unrelated files.
Log each payroll export collection, alert on anomalous retrievals, and remove or revoke access after the payroll processing window.
